minutes.headline: Master plan consultants held a public workshop on values and goals; no votes were taken and the survey's extension was left open.
minutes.summary: The consultant team led the third public master plan meeting: process overview, survey results, a values exercise in pairs, and a Brain Dash idea exercise on a town model. Residents asked about approval, funding, implementation and survey representation, and raised ideas such as a linear green on Memorial Drive and mountain bike trails. No formal votes were taken.

what_happened.line: The master plan consultants ran a public workshop on town values and goals; no votes were taken.
Whether to extend the master plan survey was left to the steering committee and the planning board chair to decide.
Residents were asked to contact Josie Gilchrist to distribute survey links and flyers through newsletters and organisations.
Asked how the plan is funded, the answer was that the state does not reimburse the town; any grants used were left unclear.
The plan will include rough order-of-magnitude costs and suggested funding sources for its recommendations.

why_it_matters: The master plan sets the priorities, such as housing, open space, parking and trails, that later zoning changes and Town Meeting spending requests are likely to cite.
Residents who want the survey to reflect more of the town have a window now, since its extension was undecided and outreach help was requested.
